title: Define f(x) once, evaluate at a point
task: Enter a given function once and read its value at a stated input.

steps.text: Type the function once as f(x)= followed by its expression.
Use the typing shortcuts for powers, roots, fractions and pi as the expression needs them.
Press Enter for a new expression line.
Type f with the input in parentheses, and the value appears in the expression list.

exam_habit.text: Using the function names given rather than copying analytic expressions keeps the grouping parentheses that a substituted expression can lose.
A value obtained from a graphing calculator without the equation, function or definite integral that was entered loses the setup point, so the setup is written beside the result.

sources.anchor_quote: Once you've defined a function, you can use it in expressions or within other functions.
Use function notation to evaluate functions for a certain value.
